newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Thai central bank says baht returning to normal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thai central bank says baht returning to normal.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Friday that speculative attacks on the baht had ended and the situation for the embattled currency was returning to normal.
"Since yesterday, there has been no speculation (in the baht). If there is any speculation we will do our duty (intervene)," Bank of Thailand deputy governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said.
"The speculation in the baht has stopped, judging from the level the baht is trading against the dollar in the market compared with the midrate," Chaiyawat said.
"Investor thinking is now on the reverse side. They are now buying the baht because they know it is not worth speculating," he added.

Attacks on the baht by foreign speculators this week forced swap rates to soar, sparked heavy Thai and other regional central bank intervention to keep the currency from sliding and sent shockwaves through the Thai stock market, which fell to near eight-year lows.
The bourse dropped 7.3 percent on the week although it recovered slightly on Friday to end up 3.32 points at 561.19.
However, forex dealers said on Friday that they had noted selling of dollars for the baht in the spot market by those seeking to ease their tight baht liquidity.

The baht weakened slightly during the day but was trading in a stable range of 25.800/25.850 to the dollar in late dealings compared to 25.300/25.340 late on Thursday. The central bank fixed the midrate at 25.82 versus the dollar.

Chaiyawat also made clear that foreign speculators who sold the baht heavily for U.S. dollars would have to pay a high price for their action by buying back the baht from the more expensive swap market to square outstanding positions.

"We separate local investors from outside speculators in terms of liquidity supply. The outside speculators cannot buy baht back to meet obligations through regular channels. For Thai business, everything will be normal," he said.

"The speculators must pay the price. Because of their speculative move, the swap premiums soared. If they intend to buy from the forward market like that, they must buy through the swap market," he added.
Local foreign exchange dealers confirmed that the central bank had told them not to buy dollars from offshore punters to fight against further speculation.
"We were informally informed (by the central bank) not to buy dollars from offshore players," said a dealer.
Chaiyawat said he expected liquidity and the overnight interbank rate in the local money market to be tight on Friday but added that the central bank was ready to help ease and calm the situation.

The local interbank rate eased to 15-18 percent late after jumping to 20-22 percent early on Friday. The morning jump came as liquidity tightened while demand for the baht rose and the baht/dollar swap premiums rocketed to around 70-100 satangs, dealers said.
Thailand has been dogged by investor jitters over its sluggish economy, which is expected to grow at just over five percent this year -- the lowest in a decade.
